tier1.note: Tier 1 is alert-grade: every line is a fact about the machine, detectable at n=1. A red is a same-day conversation, not a weekly statistic.

tier2.method: Post-move hours +1..+3 London, each metric divided by this campaign's own median for that hour-of-day over the trailing 28 days; the post-hours of one decision are averaged into a single observation (clustered by decision) before any mean or interval; arms are E1's own applied moves vs its holds, live campaigns only, accumulated over the whole E1 era rather than one week.
tier2.caveat: OBSERVATIONAL. Hour-of-day normalisation removes the diurnal shape, not selection: E1 moves precisely when the campaign is in an unusual state, so an arm gap is evidence the lever transmits, not a measured causal effect. Jitter was retired (D78), so there is no randomised instrument and there will not be one.

per_campaign.note: smallest arm has 3 decisions, floor is 20 — read as a trend, not a result
smallest arm has 10 decisions, floor is 20 — read as a trend, not a result

tier3.no_profit_verdict: This tier states no pass/fail on profit, by design. Daily P/L on these campaigns has a standard deviation of roughly $823/day against effects worth $50-150/day, so a week of data cannot tell a good week from a lucky one. Read the ranges, not the signs.

composition.note: The control group is NOT the portfolio it was: competitor, personal left it on promotion to E1 and accounted for 6.0% + 6.6% of its cost during the 4-week baseline. Both sides of the diff-in-diff are computed on today's membership, so the arithmetic is consistent — but the comparison is against a smaller, noisier account than the one earlier cards used, and every further promotion shrinks it again.

tier3.note: Comparators: (1) the campaign's own pre-E1 era, the 28 days before its first live decision; (2) diff-in-diff against the rest of the account, each side measured as this week's margin minus its own 4-week baseline, in percentage points. Neither is causal. Every figure carries the week's lead-concentration proxy, and a flagged week means the margin number should not be reasoned from at all.

limitations: No pass/fail profit verdict is possible at this scale and none is given (§3.1).

Lead concentration is an HOUR-LEVEL PROXY computed from hourly aggregates; the true top-lead share needs lead-level data (internal reporting dashboard) and is deliberately not collected by this route.
Tier 2 is observational: no randomised instrument exists since jitter was retired (D78).
Tier 3 comparators are non-causal. The rest of the account is managed by a human on a different cadence, which is a difference in kind, not just in level.
Everything is computed from the archive as it stood at the bundle timestamp; the last hour or two of the week may still be settling (~90-minute cliff, A5.1).
